sun.upright:
Aries Suns are built to go first and be seen going, so a card of a man sitting very still on four coins is an odd draw for your light. The Sun, the planet behind this card, is exalted in Aries, an honoured guest at its brightest. In this card, though, it's sitting in Capricorn, and Capricorn squares Aries. Both are cardinal signs that like to lead, and a square between them is friction that forces something to move. What it's pushing you to do is guard something you've already won.

For you that's harder than the winning was. You fought for the job, the flat, the savings, the spot on the team, and the fight was the fun part. Holding on feels like being benched. There's pride in it too, the sense that it's yours because you took it and nobody else is having it, and I see that fierce, slightly defensive grip in Aries Suns a lot. The card's planet does have a foothold in your sign. It rules the middle ten degrees, the decan of the Three of Wands, a man on a cliff watching his ships go out. That's how Aries holds best. Send it out, keep an eye on it, and don't sit on it.

At work it's the project you won't hand over, though someone else could run it and you're itching for the next one. With money it may be the first time in years you've actually kept some, and it feels oddly exposing, as if everyone can see you've got something to lose. Pick one thing you've won and write a single line about what it's actually for.
sun.reversed:
When the Four turns over for an Aries Sun, the grip usually lets go all at once, and rarely on purpose. The savings go on the new idea in one weekend. The job you guarded for two years gets quit in a single hot conversation. Or it goes the other way, and you clamp down on credit and control, running everything yourself because letting anyone else touch it feels like losing. With the Sun exalted in your sign, both versions come from pride, and both feel completely justified in the moment.

Money tends to show it first, a big spend that felt like freedom on the day and like a hole a month later. At work it's the colleague who's stopped offering to help because you never take it. Before the next big move, wait two days. If it still looks right after that, go ahead, and tell one person what you're doing before you do it.

moon.upright:
Look at the posture on this card. Arms locked round one coin, feet pinned on two more, barely able to shift his weight. For an Aries Moon that's close to a picture of what frightens you, being stuck, held down, with nowhere to put a feeling. Your Moon settles by doing something about it. Shout, run, fix it, go. So when this card turns up as your tides, it's describing a stretch where you're holding a lot in, which you're not used to, and your body knows before you do.

Earth and fire don't naturally clash or get on. They have to be introduced, and here the introduction is tense, because Capricorn squares Aries and both signs want to go first. It's like a lid on a pot. You've decided, maybe for good reasons, that this isn't the time to react, so the anger or the fear or the excitement is tucked away where nobody can see it. Aries does that badly. It leaks out sideways as short answers and a jaw that's tight by evening. There's something sensible in the card all the same. The Sun is exalted in your sign, and a feeling held for a day and then said clearly lands far better than one fired off in the first minute.

With a partner it's the thing you've been sitting on for a week. With a parent it's the old instinct to never let them see you rattled. In bed it's lying awake with your fists half closed. Go for a hard walk, and on the way home work out which one feeling actually needs saying.
moon.reversed:
Upside down, this is the lid coming off. An Aries Moon can only hold a feeling for so long, and the reversed Four is what happens when you've held one past that point. It goes in a rush. The row over nothing, the money spent to feel better, the door shut a bit harder than you meant. Or the fear of losing something takes hold and you get grabby with it, checking where your partner is, needing the plan down to the hour, which isn't like you and which you'll dislike in yourself.

Home tends to take the brunt, since it's where you let go. Friends may notice you're quicker to take offence. When you feel the pressure building, say something small and true early, while it's still small. 'I'm on edge, it's nothing you did' is plenty. Say it before dinner.

rising.upright:
Aries rising usually walks in first and asks questions later, so people who know you may find you oddly buttoned up when this card lands on your mask. The Four puts a guard on the front door. You come across as someone with something to protect, a position, a reputation, a bit of money, who isn't going to be talked out of it. Strangers pick up authority first, and the warmth later if at all.

Some of that is the Sun, which is exalted in Aries, so the card's planet is honoured at your Ascendant and gives you real weight in a room. You don't have to push. The odd part for you is the stillness. Capricorn squares Aries, and a square is friction that makes something happen, and here it's your instinct to jump in rubbing up against a card that wants you to hold your ground and wait. It feels like biting your tongue in every meeting. You can see the opening and you're letting it pass, because some part of you has decided that protecting what you've got comes first for a while.

In a negotiation, a pay rise, the price of a car, the rent, it's a real advantage, because you won't blink first. In a new team or on a first date it can read as closed, arms folded, hard to warm to, and that isn't what you're like at all. Let the stance do its work wherever there's something to bargain over. Somewhere social, say one unguarded thing in the first few minutes.
rising.reversed:
An Aries Ascendant with the Four upside down tends to swing. Either you come in defensive, bristling before anyone's said anything to bristle at, or you overcorrect and give too much away in the first ten minutes. Buying the round, offering the favour, telling the new colleague your salary. Fire likes to spend, and a reversed Four stops checking the spending. Both come from the same worry, that people won't take you seriously unless you show your hand fast.

At work it can look like prickliness in a meeting that didn't call for it. In a new friendship it's generosity that leaves you slightly out of pocket and slightly resentful. Before you walk into the next room full of strangers, decide what you're keeping to yourself. Then be as open as you like about everything else.

sun.upright:
This is one of the easiest draws a Taurus Sun can get, and that's worth being a little suspicious of. Capricorn and Taurus are both earth, four signs apart, a trine, so the card speaks your own language and turns the volume up. You want things that last and you want to be known as someone solid, someone who has enough and knows what it's worth. The card says hold on to it. You were going to anyway.

The Sun visits Taurus without any special rank and takes on the tone of Venus, your ruler, and that changes what the grip is on. A Capricorn grip is about status and safety. A Taurus one is about comfort, the good sofa, the savings that let you sleep, the routine that took years to get right. Same element, so it amplifies, for better and for too much, and it's hard to tell which is happening while you're in it. It all feels like good sense. Why change a thing that works? The trouble starts when the reserve becomes something you look at instead of something you use, and when any request to spend it, time or money or affection, feels like a small threat.

With money, this is the account you're proud of and haven't touched even for something that would make your life plainly better. At home it's the cupboard full of things kept just in case. At work it's staying put in a role that's safe and slightly too small for you, and I've seen Taurus Suns do that for a decade. Spend on one good thing, something built to last, and notice how it feels to own it.
sun.reversed:
The reversed Four on a Taurus Sun can dig in. Fixed earth already resists being moved, and when the card turns over that resistance goes possessive, over a person, a way of doing things, a piece of furniture nobody else is allowed to shift. Or Venus takes over and the loosening is all comfort. The nice dinner, the new coat, the second nice dinner, spending that feels like looking after yourself until the statement arrives.

Relationships show it in small ways, like minding very much who sits in your chair. Work shows it as refusing a change you'd probably like once you'd tried it. Choose one thing you've been holding fast to and let it be moved an inch. A new route home, a borrowed book you don't chase, dinner at their place for once.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon feels safe when the fridge is full, the bills are paid and nobody's moved anything. This card understands that completely. It's an earth card from Capricorn, trine your Moon sign, and the two of you want the same thing, enough, put by, and kept. So what it's showing is a nervous system that wants a reserve. Money in the account, food in the cupboard, a partner who's where they said they'd be.

There's a low hum of counting that comes with it. You know roughly what's in the bank without checking. You notice when the good olive oil is running low. You've quietly worked out what you'd do if the job went. None of that is anxiety exactly, and it's often very useful, but same-element pairings amplify, and a Taurus Moon with this card can slip into holding everything a bit too tightly, feelings included. You'd sooner leave the upsetting thing unsaid, because bringing it up moves things, and moving things is exactly what you're trying to avoid. The Sun here takes on Venus's colouring, which is why the grip comes out soft and pleasant, and why people don't always see it.

In your body it's shoulders that stay up and a jaw that's set by evening. With a partner it's a small jealousy you'd be embarrassed to name. The emergency fund ends up doing the job of a security blanket, which is fine until you're afraid to use it in an actual emergency. Once a day, put your hands flat on the table and let your shoulders drop. Before dinner is a good time for it.
moon.reversed:
Turned over, the card on a Taurus Moon usually means comfort's being used to hold something down. A third helping, a basket of things online, a Sunday that never leaves the sofa. Venus rules your Moon sign, and when the grip slips it slips toward pleasure, and fixed earth can keep that up for a long while without noticing. The other version is the clench, a possessiveness about people and routines so strong that any change feels like theft.

Your partner may be the first to notice, when a small change of plan gets a big reaction. The bank notices too. What are you actually trying to keep hold of? Have one conversation about it, even a short one, before you reach for anything to make it feel better.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising already looks unhurried and hard to shift, and drawing the Four for your mask makes that the whole first impression. People meet someone composed and well put together, who doesn't rush, doesn't overshare and seems to have things in hand. Some will assume you've got money whether you do or not. Capricorn is trine Taurus, earth to earth, so the card sits naturally on you and nobody will think you're putting it on.

The Sun comes into Taurus as Venus's guest, which softens the guard into good manners. You're pleasant and you're closed, and people can't quite tell where one stops and the other starts. That's useful. It's also why new people take longer to get to know you than you'd think, and why some give up. As far as you're concerned you're just being careful with a stranger. You want to see how they behave before you give them anything, and a Taurus Ascendant's idea of anything can be surprisingly small, a phone number, a real opinion, what you do on weekends.

When you're bargaining it's a gift. You name a price and sit there, and the other person fills the silence. At a new job it reads as reliability, and you'll likely be trusted with the budget or the keys early. In dating it can come across as unimpressed when you're actually quite keen. Next time you like someone, tell them one ordinary personal thing sooner than feels natural. Your favourite café is enough.
rising.reversed:
A Taurus Ascendant with this card reversed can lead with its possessions. The watch, the car, the renovation, the name of the restaurant, all offered up in the first conversation as a kind of credential. Venus is good at surfaces, and a reversed Four uses them to say you're secure without anyone asking. The other version is simply immovable. You've made your mind up about a new person inside five minutes and nothing they do shifts it.

At work it looks like the newcomer who's written off before they've had a chance. Socially it's the evening where you talked about the house and never about yourself. With a new neighbour it's the fence conversation that stays about the fence. Let the next person you meet find out one thing about you that money had nothing to do with.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns tend to hold on to options where other people hold on to money. Every door kept ajar, every contact saved, three projects on the go so none of them can trap you. The Four is a card about gripping, and for you the grip may not look like saving at all. Capricorn and Gemini are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and earth and air are opposed elements, talk against proof. What this card wants from your Sun is something you can point to.

That sits heavily with you. You're good at being quick and interesting, and your pride is in being the bright one, the one who knows. The card is saying pick a thing and keep it, build it up, let it get solid enough to be judged. There's a fact on your side here. The Sun rules the last ten degrees of Gemini, the decan of the Ten of Swords, the card where all the talking finally runs out and something has to be accepted as done. If your Sun sits late in the sign you'll know that feeling well. For every Gemini Sun, though, the adjusting is constant and small, and each time you commit, part of you wants to renegotiate.

In a job it's being the freelancer with six clients and no pension, or the salaried one who's bored and won't leave. The savings plan gets started every January and spent by March on something interesting. In friendship it's a phone full of people you'd love to see and don't. Which of your projects would still matter to you in five years? Give that one three months with no new ideas added.
sun.reversed:
When the Four reverses on a Gemini Sun, money and energy tend to go the way of your attention, in lots of directions at once. Small subscriptions, a course half done, a tenner lent that you won't ask back. The Sun takes its colour from Mercury in your sign, and with the card upside down that quickness turns loose and leaky. Or it turns guarded in a very Gemini way, holding on to information, keeping the useful bit back so you stay the one who knows.

At work that second version shows as the colleague who won't share the spreadsheet. At home the first one shows on the bank statement. Pick one leak, a subscription or a habit, and close it. Then tell somebody at work the thing you've been keeping to yourself.

moon.upright:
Most feelings, for a Gemini Moon, don't feel real until they've been said to someone. That's how you settle. A long phone call, a voice note, a chat at the kitchen bench that goes round in circles until you've found the shape of the thing. This card on your Moon is about keeping, and what it tends to show here is a stretch where you're keeping things to yourself that you'd normally have talked out by lunchtime.

Earth and air are opposed elements, idea against matter, and the quincunx between Capricorn and Gemini means the two keep having to adjust around each other. It's like a word you can't find. You've got the feeling, and it's heavier than your usual weather, and every time you go to say it out loud something in you decides it's private. Some of that is healthy. A Gemini Moon can talk a feeling into something lighter before it's actually been felt, and this card slows that down. Some of it is fear, a worry that if you say it, it'll become true, or get repeated.

Sleep usually shows it, a mind still running at midnight with nowhere to put what it's thinking. With friends it's the chat where you ask all the questions and give nothing back. With a partner it's a flatness they can sense without knowing what it's about. Write it down by hand, on paper that stays in a drawer. Then decide whether anyone else needs to read it.
moon.reversed:
Upside down on a Gemini Moon, the card usually means the holding has gone into your head. What you're hoarding is facts. Reading everything there is about a worry, refreshing the news, checking the account balance four times in an afternoon, as if knowing more would make it safe. Or the lid comes off all at once and you tell far too many people far too much, then feel exposed for days.

Your phone is the evidence, both ways. The group chat might notice you've gone quiet, or that you've said something you'd normally keep. Give the worrying part of your mind a fixed ten minutes to look things up. Outside that, leave the phone in another room, and if a friend asks how you are, tell them one thing and stop there.

rising.upright:
There's a card on your front door that doesn't talk much, and Gemini rising usually does. People who meet you under the Four of Pentacles find someone more measured and harder to read than they'd expected. Still quick, still watching everything, but holding back the easy chat. You're giving out less and taking in a lot. It can come across as cool, or as if you know something they don't.

The Sun is only visiting Gemini, taking its colour from Mercury, so what's guarded here is mostly information. Your plans, your opinion of the person in front of you, what you earn, what you're after. Capricorn is quincunx Gemini, and air and earth pull against each other, so this doesn't sit naturally. You'll feel the jokes arrive and then decide to keep them in. You're weighing every sentence for what it gives away, which is tiring for a sign that likes to think out loud, and I've seen Gemini risings come out of a stretch like this oddly drained without knowing why.

It works brilliantly in an interview or anywhere you're being assessed, because you give tight, clean answers and nothing that can be used against you. In a new friendship it slows everything down, and you might come away thinking they didn't like you when they just couldn't get a read. With a new manager it's how you get taken seriously. At the next social thing, let one joke out early, a real one, and watch the room loosen.
rising.reversed:
With Gemini rising, the reversed Four tends to leak. A guard that's usually up comes down in the first conversation, and you hear yourself sharing the salary, the gossip, the thing a friend told you in confidence, because it made a good story. Mercury colours the Sun on your Ascendant and it loves a good story. The other version is cagey. Short answers, changing the subject, a stranger left feeling you've something to hide.

This shows up at work as saying too much to the wrong person in a first meeting. Socially it's the story that gets back to its owner. With a new neighbour it's your whole last relationship told over the fence. Before the next introduction, pick one topic you won't go near, and stay off it however good the story is.

sun.upright:
Cancer and Capricorn sit opposite each other, and the Four of Pentacles is a Capricorn card, so this draw is your sign looking across its own axis at its opposite number. The pull there is toward balance. Home at one end, the world and its ladders at the other. Family and feeling on your side, status and savings on Capricorn's. A Cancer Sun wants to keep its people safe and be seen as the one who does. This card says do it with money and walls.

The Sun visits Cancer without special dignity, taking its colour from the Moon, so whatever you're gripping has feeling all through it. It's rarely only money. It's the house because of who grew up in it. It's the savings because of what they'd mean for your kids, or your mother, or the partner who isn't very good with cash. Earth and water get on well, each giving the other shape, and so this holding feels right to you, even virtuous. The catch is how much you keep for the family and how little for yourself. You can be a fortress for everyone else and still be sleeping badly because there's no room in the fortress for you.

At home it's the parent who can't quite let a grown child manage their own mistakes. With money it's a long list of things saved for and nothing on it with your name. At work it's staying in a job you've outgrown because it pays the mortgage. Set aside a small amount that's only for you, and spend it without explaining it to anyone.
sun.reversed:
With the Four upside down, a Cancer Sun can start holding people the way the card holds coins. Checking in a bit too often, keeping the family close by keeping them slightly dependent, making every decision in the house because you trust your judgement over theirs. The Moon rules your sign, so all of this comes wrapped in care, and it's very hard to see while you're doing it. The other version is giving everything away until the reserve's gone and you're quietly resentful.

The family table is usually where it shows. At work it can be mothering a team that would do better if you let them fail a bit. Ask a grown child, a partner or a colleague what they'd actually like from you. Give them that, and only that, for a month.

moon.upright:
Somewhere in your house there's probably a box. Letters, a hospital bracelet, a child's drawing, a scarf that still smells of someone. A Cancer Moon keeps things because they hold the feeling, and this is a card of keeping. That's the first thing it's pointing at, what you've kept, and how much of your sense of safety depends on it staying exactly where it is.

The Moon rules your sign, and the card's Sun visits with no dignity of its own, so it takes on the Moon's colouring. Its Capricorn side sits across the axis from you, an opposition, a pull toward balance. So there's a practical, cold-weather part of this card that doesn't suit you, the part that counts and budgets, and a tender part that suits you very well. Water and earth are friendly elements, and what grows between them grows slowly and holds. Safety, for you, is having enough. Enough money, enough food, enough of the people you love within reach. When any of that feels uncertain you tighten around what's left, and you hold people a little closer than they'd like.

In the kitchen it's the freezer stocked for a siege. With a partner it's needing to know when they'll be home, and minding when they're late far beyond what you'd say out loud. With your mother, or whoever raised you, it's an old fear of there not being enough that you took on without choosing it. Go through one drawer. Keep what still means something, and let one item go.
moon.reversed:
A Cancer Moon with the card reversed tends to hold on to hurt. The comment from years ago, the Christmas that went wrong, the friend who didn't ring when it mattered. Water keeps, and a reversed Four stops letting anything go, so old feelings get stored with the same care as the good china. Sometimes it flips into a purge, the whole wardrobe to the op shop in one grim afternoon, and then a week of regret.

Family is the obvious place it shows. Sleep is another, because the old stuff surfaces at night. Pick one grudge that's more than a year old and ask yourself honestly whether the other person even knows about it. If they don't, think about whether you still need to carry it.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising already comes with a shell, and this card gives the shell a lock. People meeting you find someone pleasant, careful and quite private, the kind of person who asks about them and says very little about themselves. There's a point about your chart that makes the card land harder than it might. With Cancer on the Ascendant, Capricorn is on your seventh house, the house of partners and the person across the table. So the card's sign is the sign of the other people in your life.

That means this draw is as much about who you're meeting as how you're meeting them. You may be dealing with somebody guarded, careful with money, slow to trust, and you're matching them, shell for shell. Earth and water suit each other and things between them grow slowly and hold, so it isn't a bad pairing. It's just slow. You're waiting for them to go first, and they're waiting for you, and you both go home thinking the other one's a bit cold.

In business it's a negotiation where both sides are polite and nobody names a number. In dating it's four dates in and nobody's said anything real. With a new landlord or employer it's the contract read twice, by both of you. Somebody has to open a hand first. Decide it'll be you, in something small, a real opinion or a bit of your history, and watch what they do with it.
rising.reversed:
For Cancer rising, the reversed Four can make the first minutes awkward. The shell snaps shut at the wrong moment, so a stranger who was being friendly gets a polite nothing and decides you don't like them. Or it goes the other way and you open far too wide, offering help, lending things, taking on a newcomer's problems the day you meet them, then retreating hard when it all gets to be too much. Capricorn sits on your seventh house, so the people you meet may be guarded too, and they'll take the retreat personally.

At work it looks like the new colleague you mothered for a fortnight and now avoid in the corridor. In romance it's warm on the first date and unreachable by the third. Find a steady middle setting for new people, friendly, a little bit of yourself, and nothing you'll want back.

sun.upright:
Look at where the man on this card has put his fourth coin. It's balanced on top of his crown. For a Leo Sun that detail's hard to miss, because the Sun rules Leo, it's at home there, and in this card the Sun is sitting in Capricorn's closing degrees. So it's your own ruler talking, with the authority of your sign's landlord, and it's saying something Leos don't much like hearing. Keep some back.

Leo is fixed fire and gives generously. Paying for dinner, lavish presents, the big gesture, your whole warmth on show, and your pride is bound up in being the one who can afford to give. Capricorn and Leo are quincunx, five signs apart with nothing in common, and earth and fire have to be introduced before they'll cooperate. Holding back feels like dimming. You'll notice a sort of stinginess in yourself you don't recognise and don't like. But the Sun in Capricorn is still the Sun, and what it wants from you is a reserve, so that your light doesn't depend on being topped up by applause or by other people's gratitude.

Money-wise it's the Leo habit of treating everyone, and finally letting someone else pay. With creative work it's keeping a project private until it's properly finished, which will feel almost physically wrong. With a child, or someone you mentor, it's letting them have their moment without adding yours to it. Choose one thing you'd normally show off early, a bit of work or some good news, and keep it to yourself for a fortnight.
sun.reversed:
The Sun rules Leo, so when its card turns over for a Leo Sun, pride takes the wheel. One version is grand spending, paying for everyone's evening to be sure you're the host. The other is hoarding the credit, the spotlight, the best ideas, and getting sharp with anyone who threatens to shine a bit too. Underneath each is the same worry, that there's only so much warmth to go round and you need to hold on to your share.

At work it's the project you won't let a junior present. With friends it's keeping a tab you'd be embarrassed to admit to. With a partner it's needing to be the generous one, always. Let someone else take the bill, or the credit, in the same week, and just say thank you.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon settles when it's loved out loud. Being noticed, being chosen, being told. With this card on your tides, the question is what you do when that attention feels scarce, and the honest answer for a lot of Leo Moons is that you start holding your own warmth back until someone proves they deserve it. The Sun rules your Moon sign, and here it's parked in Capricorn, cool and careful, which is a strange mood for a fire Moon to be in.

The aspect between them is a quincunx, the constant small adjustment of two signs with no common ground. It feels like pride with a lock on it. You'd love to say you missed them, and you won't, because they didn't say it first. You'd love to throw the party, and you're waiting to see who'd come. Loyalty is one of the best things about a Leo Moon, and the card can turn it a little possessive, keeping close the people who've shown up for you and a bit jealous of anyone else they spend time with.

With a partner it's affection rationed until they've earned it back. With close friends it's minding, far beyond what you'll let on, who got invited to what. With your own children, if you have them, it's wanting to be the favourite. Next time, say the warm thing first, before you know how it'll land.
moon.reversed:
When this card reverses on a Leo Moon, hurt pride goes into storage. You stop offering the warmth you'd usually pour out, and you tell yourself it's self-respect. Or it tips into a bid for reassurance, the grand gesture, the expensive present, the big declaration, made partly so the other person will have to give something back. The Sun, your Moon's ruler, sits in a cold sign here, and upside down it can make love feel like a transaction.

Partners feel it first, as a sulk nobody can find the cause of. Friends feel it as a coolness after an event you felt left out of. Tell the person who hurt you, plainly and without drama, what it was. Then let it be finished, and don't bring it up in the next argument.

rising.upright:
With Leo rising, the Sun is your chart ruler, the planet that steers the whole chart, and this card puts it in Capricorn with four coins held tight. So what's on your mask speaks for the thing that drives you. People are meeting a more regal version of you than usual. Composed, well dressed, a bit expensive-looking, clearly someone who has something and knows its value, with less of the easy warmth that usually gets you liked in the first minute.

Leo rising is fixed fire and tends to arrive like the evening's host. Capricorn is quincunx Leo and earth and fire need introducing, so the card and your Ascendant don't blend. They sit side by side. What comes out is dignity with the door shut. It may feel to you like being guarded for good reasons, maybe after being taken advantage of, or after a stretch of giving too much of yourself to people who didn't return it. Strangers read it as confidence, and some read it as a wall.

In a job interview or a pitch this is strong. You look like someone worth paying properly. On a date it's poised and slightly hard to reach. In a new group of friends it's being admired first and liked a good while later. Go into the next social thing with one generous act planned, something small, a compliment you mean or a round you buy, and do it early.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with the Four reversed may be spending to be seen. The good bottle brought to dinner, the expensive haircut before the interview, the round bought for people you've only just met. None of that's wrong in itself, except that it's standing in for you. The Sun rules your Ascendant, so whatever you project comes out loud. Or it goes the other way, a coolness at the door so marked that people think you're arrogant when you're actually wary.

It shows in money first, a card bill full of first impressions. At work it can be a new team deciding you're aloof in week one. Next time you meet someone new, bring nothing to impress them with. Turn up as yourself, and ask about them before you mention anything you own.

sun.upright:
The Sun rules the first ten degrees of Virgo, the decan of the Eight of Pentacles, where an apprentice sits at a bench carving the same coin over and over until it's right. That's this card's foothold in your sign, and it says a lot about how a Virgo Sun holds things. You hold on to the method. Capricorn is trine Virgo, earth to earth, so the card speaks your language, and it amplifies whatever's already there, the care and the control both.

What you want is to be useful and good at it, and to be seen as good at it. The Four says protect that. Keep the standards. Don't let anyone rush you or cut the corner. It all seems perfectly reasonable until you notice you haven't let anyone else touch the work in months. The Sun visiting Virgo takes its colour from Mercury, so the grip is on detail, on knowing how things work, and on being the only one who knows. That's a kind of hoarding too. Give it to someone else and they might do it wrong. Or right, which in some ways would be worse.

At work it's not delegating, and being tired and a little superior about it. With money it's the careful budget kept in a spreadsheet only you understand. With your health it's routines followed so strictly that a missed session feels like a failure. Teach one thing you know to someone who could use it, properly, and let them do it their way afterwards.
sun.reversed:
The reversed Four on a Virgo Sun is the grip gone anxious. You can see every way things could go wrong, so you hold on to everything, the task, the money, the plan, and check it over and over. Nothing leaves your hands until it's perfect, which means a lot never leaves them at all. Occasionally it flips, and you give your time away so freely to other people's problems that there's none left for your own work.

This lands at work as a queue of things nearly finished. At home it lands as help for everybody and nothing asked for yourself. Send one thing out at the stage you'd usually call a draft. See what comes back before you touch it again, and notice how little of what worried you anyone mentions.

moon.upright:
Order is how a Virgo Moon feels safe. The list made, the bag packed the night before, the kitchen wiped down before bed. Capricorn trines Virgo and both are earth, so this card lands on your Moon like it belongs there, and it amplifies your need to have things under control, for better and for too much. There's comfort in it. There's also a tightness you may have stopped noticing.

The Sun comes into Virgo as a guest and takes on Mercury's habits, so the holding is mental as well as practical. You're keeping track. Of money, of what's in the cupboard, of what you said at the meeting and whether it came across wrong. It feels like being responsible, and mostly you are, but the card is showing the point where keeping track turns into holding on, when a missed routine or an unexpected bill sets off a lot of worry for its size. Virgo's own card is The Hermit, and there's a quiet, private sort of self-protection going on here, something you'd like to sort out alone before anyone sees.

In your body it's a stomach that knots when plans change, and shoulders that ache by Friday. With a partner it's showing love by managing everything, and struggling when they want to manage something themselves. The bank app gets checked several times a day. Choose one small thing a day to leave undone. An unmade bed, an unanswered email, a dish in the sink overnight.
moon.reversed:
A Virgo Moon with the Four reversed is holding on with its teeth. The routines have gone rigid. The budget's become a set of rules you can't break without feeling awful. You worry about money you actually have, and about losing a job that isn't in any danger. Or, after weeks of that, everything slides at once, the diet, the cleaning, the spending, and then you feel worse for it.

You'll see it in your sleep and in your temper with the people you live with. Say the actual number or the actual scenario out loud to someone you trust. Let them ask you questions about it, and answer them honestly, including the ones that make you feel a bit silly.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising tends to come across as tidy, capable and slightly reserved, and with this card drawn for your mask, people are meeting the most buttoned-up version of you. Neat, prepared, quietly competent, giving away very little. Capricorn's trine to Virgo means the card fits you easily, same element, and nobody will think it's an act. They'll just assume you're very private, and very good at your job.

The Sun visits Virgo as Mercury's guest, and on the Ascendant that shows as care over every word you use with a stranger. You're working out how much to say, what they'll do with it, whether it's wise. It seems like simple caution to you, and you might not notice how much you're holding back until someone says they found you hard to read. Pisces is on your seventh house, the sign opposite, and that's the sign of the people who come towards you. Pisces is sextile Capricorn, so there's an easy opening for someone softer, someone who doesn't mind going first. They'll get further with you than you'd expect.

At a job interview this is excellent, since you look like someone who'd never lose the paperwork. At a new workplace it earns trust quickly and friendship slowly. With a neighbour it's years of polite nodding. Tell one new person something that isn't about work, something you enjoy or something you're hopeless at.
rising.reversed:
When Virgo rising draws this card reversed, the reserve can come off as judgement. You notice the stain on the shirt, the typo in the email, the wrong fork, and even if you say nothing your face may say it for you. People feel inspected. The other version is modesty that goes too far, undervaluing yourself in a first meeting, naming a low price, playing down the degree. The card's grip has moved on to your sense of worth, and a Virgo Ascendant tends to guard that by getting small or getting critical.

At work this is the pay you didn't ask for. Socially it's the stranger who thinks you disapprove of them. Next time you're asked what you do or what you charge, give a full answer and stop, without a qualifier at the end.

sun.upright:
The Sun is in fall in Libra, which means it's uncomfortable there and struggles to be heard, so it has to get its work done by an indirect route. That matters when this card turns up for a Libra Sun, because the Four is about the self holding on to what's its own, and a Libra Sun finds 'mine' a hard word to say. You're here to make things fair and to be liked while you do it. Keeping something just for you can feel like a failure of manners.

Capricorn squares Libra, two cardinal signs pushing at each other, and air and earth pull opposite ways, talk against proof. So there's friction. Part of you wants to keep the peace and share everything evenly. Part of you, lately, wants to keep the house, the savings, the Saturday, and is annoyed about wanting it. Because the Sun's in fall, you're likely to hold on sideways. Keeping score quietly. Staying in a relationship because leaving would mean dividing things. Being charming about a boundary you'd really like to state flatly.

With a partner, it's the shared account that's become a quiet source of tension, and who pays for what. At work it's hanging on to a role for the title, when the job itself has gone stale. With friends it's always splitting the bill to the cent. Say one plain sentence about something that's yours and isn't up for negotiation, and don't soften it with a joke.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun with the Four upside down may be giving too much away to keep things even. Paying over your share so nobody feels awkward, agreeing to the holiday you can't afford, handing over the credit at work because arguing about it feels ugly. The Sun in fall doesn't push for itself easily. Then, eventually, a resentful tally starts in your head, and it comes out all at once over something tiny.

Couples feel this most, around money or around whose family gets Christmas. At work it's the promotion you stood aside for. Work out what a fair share actually is for you, in dollars or hours, and write it down. Then hold to it once, politely, and see what happens.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon needs things to be pleasant between people. Arguments at home get under your skin in a way others don't always understand, and you'll give up quite a lot to get the peace back. This card lands on that as a card of holding in. You're keeping your feelings very carefully to yourself, mostly to stop them upsetting anyone.

Air and earth are opposed elements, and Capricorn squares Libra, so there's friction here that forces something. The Sun, in fall in your Moon's sign, has trouble speaking up for what it needs, and it's gone quiet and careful instead. It's an odd mix. You're calm on the surface and quite tight underneath, like someone carrying a full glass across a crowded room. You're guarding the atmosphere. You're also guarding something of your own that you haven't worked out how to say without tipping the balance.

With a partner it's being agreeable about everything and feeling slightly lonely with it. With a close friend it's the thing that bothered you months ago and still hasn't been mentioned. In your body it's a tension that doesn't shift even on a nice evening. Let one small disagreement happen out loud, about where to eat or what to watch, and stay in the room while it's happening.
moon.reversed:
With this card reversed on a Libra Moon, the peacekeeping has turned into a kind of hoarding. You're storing up every small unfairness, silently, because saying any of them would cause a scene. Venus rules the sign, and there can be comfort-buying too, the pretty thing that makes a bad week feel nicer. Or you cling to a relationship that isn't working because the thought of splitting up, and dividing everything, is worse than staying.

A partner may sense the stored-up list without ever seeing it. Friends might find you pleasant and a little absent. Your bank sees the pretty things. Pick the oldest item on the list and raise it, gently, with the person concerned. Choose a calm evening, and keep to that one item.

rising.upright:
Libra rising walks in with grace and makes everyone feel at ease, and when the Four is your mask card, that ease comes with a touch of reserve. People meet someone polished, well mannered, lovely to talk to, and hard to get close to. The Sun is in fall in Libra, so the card's planet doesn't find your Ascendant comfortable, and the confidence it brings has to come through sideways. It comes out as poise, good clothes and a firm handshake, with very little said about you.

There's a chart detail here too. With Libra rising, Aries sits on your seventh house, the one for partners and the people you deal with one to one, and the Sun is exalted in Aries. So the card's planet does beautifully in the other person and struggles in you. Capricorn squares both ends of that axis. It can feel as if someone else is holding the cards, and you're being gracious about it while quietly keeping your own counsel.

In negotiations this is being charming and giving nothing away, which works. In dating it's attracting confident, direct people and staying slightly guarded with them. At a new job it's being liked by everyone and known by nobody. Say what you want at the start of the next important conversation, before the charm takes over.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising with the card reversed can over-give at the door. Offering to help before you're asked, agreeing to a price you know is too low, making yourself so accommodating that people don't quite register you. The Sun's in fall in your rising sign, and with the card upside down it can leave you feeling you have to earn your place in every room. The other version is a cool, polished front so carefully kept that nobody gets past the pleasantries.

At work it shows up as being given everything nobody else wants, because you said yes so nicely. Socially it's an evening of being delightful and going home tired and slightly empty. Let the next stranger find you a little less agreeable than usual. Disagree once, politely, and see how it lands.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns already know how to hold something close. Secrets, money, a grudge, a plan nobody else has heard. This card doesn't have to teach you anything there. Capricorn is sextile Scorpio, an easy, cooperative angle, and earth and water are friendly elements that give each other shape and hold. So the card fits you well, and the real question is whether it fits you too well.

What you want is depth and control, to know what's really going on and to be the one who decides what happens next. The Sun visits Scorpio as a guest of Mars, or of Pluto if you use the modern ruler, and the grip picks up that intensity. It doesn't feel like hoarding to you. It feels like strategy. You're keeping your cards close because the last time you didn't, somebody used them. The Sun also rules the middle ten degrees of Scorpio, the decan of the Six of Cups, where one child hands another a cup full of flowers in an old courtyard. For some Scorpio Suns what's being held here isn't money at all. It's an old loyalty, or an old wound, from a long way back.

With shared money, a joint account, an inheritance, a business with a partner, it's knowing exactly where every dollar is and not quite saying. At work it's power held quietly, the knowledge that makes you hard to replace. With someone you love it's the one thing you've never told them. Of everything you're keeping, how much is protecting you, and how much is just habit?
sun.reversed:
The Four reversed on a Scorpio Sun can turn control into possession. You're watching the joint account, checking who your partner's been talking to, keeping the information that gives you the upper hand at work. Or it swings the other way, as fixed water sometimes does, and you let go of something all at once, closing the account, ending the friendship, cutting a person off in one clean stroke. Neither feels dramatic while you're doing it. It feels decisive, which is why it's hard to catch.

The place to watch is anything shared, money or trust. Ask yourself whether the last big decision you made about someone else was yours to make alone. If it wasn't, go back and talk to them about it.

moon.upright:
There's a place a Scorpio Moon keeps its feelings where hardly anyone's allowed. That privacy is how you stay safe, and this card on your tides describes it closely. You're holding a lot in, carefully, and you've decided who gets to see it, which might well be nobody.

Capricorn sextiles Scorpio, and water and earth get on, so the card doesn't fight you. It sits with you. That's a comfort in one way. Holding steady is what you need when feelings run as deep as yours, and the card backs you on it. The difficulty is that a sextile only opens a door, it doesn't walk you through, and a Scorpio Moon with this card can hold on long after it's stopped helping. It feels like strength, like being the one who doesn't fall apart. You can keep a straight face through a great deal. Somewhere underneath, though, what you're keeping is costing you sleep, or patience, or closeness with someone who'd like to help.

In intimacy it's letting someone close physically and keeping the rest behind glass. With family it's the old story nobody's allowed to bring up. With money it's a private stash, however small, that nobody else knows about and that makes you feel safe in a way you'd find hard to explain. Tell one person one true thing about how you've been. Keep it brief if you need to, and don't apologise for it afterwards.
moon.reversed:
A Scorpio Moon under the reversed Four holds on to hurt with real skill. The betrayal from years back is filed and dated. A partner's small lapse gets added to the file. The Sun, a guest of Mars here, gives the grip heat, and the feeling you're keeping starts to run the way you treat people. Or the dam goes, and you tell someone everything in one night and regret it for a month.

It shows in jealousy that won't be argued with, and in sleep broken by the same thoughts. Before you act on the story you've been carrying, check one fact of it with the person involved. Take their answer at face value for a few days before you decide what it meant.

rising.upright:
People who meet Scorpio rising already sense something's being held back, and with this card on your mask they're right. You come across as contained, watchful and hard to read, and clearly in control of yourself. The card sits comfortably on you. Capricorn is sextile Scorpio, earth and water help each other, and nothing here needs forcing.

With Scorpio rising, Taurus sits on your seventh house, and Taurus is trine Capricorn, so the people you tend to meet and pair up with are often earthy, steady, good with money, holding types themselves. That's part of what this draw is about. The Sun visits your Ascendant as a guest of Mars, which puts some intensity behind the reserve. You're not giving anything away until you know what someone wants. You're reading them, their clothes, their manners, what they're really asking for, while telling them almost nothing.

In business this makes you a formidable first meeting, and people often come away assuming there's serious money or power behind you. In dating it's magnetic and slightly frightening, and the other person may leave without knowing whether you liked them. With a new neighbour or colleague it's the reputation for being hard to crack. Let one person see you laugh early, properly, at something that's actually funny.
rising.reversed:
Scorpio rising with the card reversed can go cold at the door. Strangers get a flat, assessing look and a short answer, and decide you're unfriendly or sizing them up, which you are. Sometimes it goes the other way, and you drop the guard with the wrong person at the wrong time, telling a near stranger things about your money or your past that you'd hesitate to tell a friend.

At work this shows in how new colleagues act, keeping their distance and choosing their words. With someone you're dating it's a test they don't know they're sitting. Choose one new person and give them the benefit of the doubt for a month. Watch what they do with it, and try not to keep score while you watch.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius sits right next door to Capricorn, and this card comes from Capricorn, so it's your neighbour's way of doing things turning up in your light. Neighbouring signs like these share very little, and each has what the other lacks. You've got the faith, the generosity, the appetite for more. Capricorn has the patience and the savings. The card asks a Sagittarius Sun to hold on to something, and 'hold on' is about the least natural phrase in your vocabulary.

The Sun visits your sign as a guest of Jupiter, and Jupiter likes to spend, to give, to say yes to the trip. So the grip here is an effort. Earth and fire are neutral and need introducing, and it can feel like someone's tied a rope to your ankle. What you're being asked to keep is often something that would let you go further later. Savings for the move, the degree you're halfway through, a relationship that's asking you to stay put for a while. Your pride is in freedom, and the card is pointing out, a bit unromantically, that freedom takes money and time and some staying.

With money it's the travel fund you keep raiding. With study it's finishing the course you started for the love of it and got bored of. With a partner it's saying yes to a lease, a joint account, a plan longer than a season. Put a fixed amount aside each week for something far off that you actually want, and leave it alone until you're ready to go.
sun.reversed:
When the card reverses for a Sagittarius Sun, the grip usually just gives. Money goes on the flight, the course, the round for the whole bar, and the reserve that was meant to make the big plan possible disappears into a lot of small good times. Jupiter colours the Sun here, and upside down that can mean generosity past what you've got. Occasionally it's the opposite, a stubborn hold on an opinion you've outgrown.

Money is the usual evidence. With a partner it's the big plans that keep being announced with nothing set aside for them. Friends may notice you arguing a position you don't really believe any more. Before the next spend over a set amount, sleep on it. If it still excites you in the morning, go ahead.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room, something to look forward to, and a sense that the future's open. This is a card of sitting still and holding tight, and on your tides it can feel like being fenced in. Capricorn is the sign next door, a semi-sextile, and the two have very little in common. Earth and fire are neutral. So this is an unfamiliar mood for you. Careful, a bit worried about money, keeping your options closed for once.

The Sun is visiting your Moon sign as Jupiter's guest, which gives it some of Jupiter's appetite, and that's why the holding pinches. You'll know it as a caution you can't shake. You're checking the balance before booking anything. You're staying in when you'd usually go. You're less sure the future will simply sort itself out, and for a Sagittarius Moon that faith is a big part of feeling safe. The card doesn't take it away. It asks you to put something solid under it, and your Moon finds that faintly insulting.

In your body it shows as restlessness, bad sleep, an urge to walk it off. With a partner it's a sudden need to talk about money that surprises you both. With friends it's saying no to a trip for once, and feeling oddly proud of it. Take one thing you're looking forward to and plan it properly, dates, costs, a budget. Knowing it's paid for may settle you in a way the daydreaming never quite does.
moon.reversed:
With the Four reversed, a Sagittarius Moon may be spending to feel free. The late booking, the big night out, the present for a friend you can't really afford, anything that makes the walls feel further away. Jupiter's influence on the Sun here makes it generous, and upside down it gets careless. Or the fear flips and you cling to a plan or a person because you're frightened of what's out there without it, which doesn't suit you at all.

The bank shows the first. Your mood shows the second, as a low, trapped irritability. What is the spending or the clinging trying to fix? Once you've got an answer, try one free thing that gives you the same feeling of space, a long walk somewhere you've never been.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising usually comes in laughing, friendly and a bit loud. With this card on your mask, strangers are meeting a quieter, more careful person than your friends would recognise. You're holding back, weighing people up, and not offering to pay. People might take it for coldness, though what's really going on is Capricorn caution sitting on a Sagittarius doorway, two neighbouring signs with little in common.

The Sun comes into Sagittarius as Jupiter's guest and brings some warmth with it, so you don't come across as unfriendly, only as someone who's thinking. Earth and fire have to be introduced, and that's what it's like. You'd love to launch into the story, promise the weekend away, offer your spare room. Something stops you, maybe a recent time you were too open-handed and it cost you. So you're watching first. People sense there's more to you than you're showing, and some find that intriguing.

In a new job this makes you look sensible, and it may get you trusted with something important earlier than usual. Travelling, it's being the one who checks the refund policy, for once. In dating it's a first date where they do most of the talking. Keep the caution for money and contracts, and let the rest of your usual warmth back into the room.
rising.reversed:
A Sagittarius Ascendant with this card reversed tends to promise too much too early. The spare room offered to someone you met an hour ago, the loan, the grand plan to go into business together. Jupiter's generosity goes out the front door with nothing held back. With a new friend it's lending the car before you know how they drive. Or the caution gets stuck, and you come across as guarded and a little preachy about money, which doesn't sound like you at all.

At work it's the deadline you agreed to in the first meeting and now can't meet. Socially it's the favour you offered freely and now regret. Make it a rule for a while that nothing gets promised until the second meeting.

sun.upright:
This card is one of Capricorn's own. The Four of Pentacles belongs to the final ten degrees of your sign, the stretch the Sun rules, so if you were born in those last days before Aquarius takes over, it's your decan card, and even if you weren't, it's speaking your language exactly. You want to build something that lasts and be respected for it. The card is a picture of that, done well and held on to hard.

The Sun only visits Capricorn, with no special dignity, and takes on Saturn's colouring. That's why the identity in this card is so bound up with what's been earned. You are who you are because of what you've built, and the fear under it is losing the building. Same element, so it amplifies, for better and for too much. The holding feels like responsibility, and plenty of it genuinely is. But Capricorn's big card is The Devil, the one with the loose chains, and this is its milder cousin, a grip you could let go of and don't, because letting go feels like the first step toward everything falling down.

At work it's the role you've guarded for years and could hand on. With money it's savings that have become a number to protect instead of something to use. With your family it's being the one who holds everything up and quietly resenting that nobody offers to take a corner. Think of one thing you're holding that you could delegate, sell or give away. Do it, and watch whether anything actually falls.
sun.reversed:
The Four reversed on a Capricorn Sun often shows up as working to protect something you've stopped enjoying. The title, the house, the portfolio, the reputation, held so tight there's no room left to live in any of it. Saturn colours the Sun in your sign, and upside down that turns into a fearful kind of thrift, saving the good wine for an occasion that never comes. Occasionally it flips into a sudden, uncharacteristic splurge that frightens you far more than it should.

At work it's hours spent defending a position. At home it's being too tired to enjoy what those hours paid for. Open the good bottle, book the good table, use the thing you've been saving. Do it on an ordinary Tuesday.

moon.upright:
Feeling safe, for a Capricorn Moon, usually means feeling in control. Bills paid ahead, a plan for the worst case, nobody able to catch you out. This card comes from your own sign, its last ten degrees, and shares its element, so it speaks straight to the part of you that needs a reserve before it can relax. Saturn rules your Moon sign, and the Sun in this card takes Saturn's colouring, which makes this about as close a match as the card gets.

Safe, for you, means having something put by and not needing anyone. Asking for help costs you more than going without. That's the card's grip, and it's in the feelings too. You keep your worries to yourself until they're solved, then mention them in passing as if they were nothing. Same-element pairings amplify, and with this one it can go past sensible into lonely, a reserve kept so carefully that nobody gets near it, including people who love you and would like to be useful. You'll know the moment when a partner asks what's wrong and you say 'nothing' out of reflex.

In the body it's a tightness through the neck and shoulders you've had so long you think it's posture. The buffer in the bank stays untouched even when spending it would clearly be the grown-up thing. With a parent, often, it's an old lesson about coping alone. Next time something's worrying you, tell someone before you've fixed it, while it's still a mess.
moon.reversed:
A Capricorn Moon with the Four reversed goes into lockdown. Feelings held so tightly they come out as tiredness or cold efficiency. You're counting, planning, cutting back, and none of it makes you feel any safer, because the threat lives mostly in your head, left over from an older time when things genuinely were short. Now and then the grip slips and there's a rare spending spree, then days of guilt.

Sleep and patience both suffer. A partner may feel shut out and not know why. Check the fear against the facts on paper, the actual numbers, with someone else looking at them too. You may find you're guarding against a shortage that ended years ago.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising already comes across as serious, capable and older than your years, and this card on your mask adds weight. It's native to your sign, one of Capricorn's three decan cards, the one the Sun rules, so it sits on your Ascendant as if it had been measured for it. People meet someone composed, well turned out, obviously competent and obviously careful. Strangers may guess you're a few years older than you are, and that you're good with money.

Saturn rules your Ascendant, which makes it your chart ruler, and the Sun in this card visits your sign under Saturn's colouring. It all points the same way, and same-element pairings don't soften each other. The reserve feels like professionalism. You don't give away what you're earning, what you think of the boss, or what you'd do if the deal fell through. That serves you. The cost is warmth. People can find you hard to relax around, and the few who get past the front are often surprised by how funny you are.

In an interview this is ideal, and in any negotiation you're hard to beat. In a new team it gets you handed responsibility early and invited to drinks late. On a date it can feel a bit like a business meeting to the other person. Let one personal thing slip in the first half hour. A hobby, a family story, a bad joke.
rising.reversed:
When this card turns over on a Capricorn Ascendant, the professional front can harden into something cold. Saturn runs your chart, and reversed, this card can make every introduction feel like an audition. People meet you and feel judged on their shoes, their title, their use to you. Or the front slips unexpectedly, and you say more than you meant to in a first meeting, about money or family, then spend days feeling exposed.

Colleagues may see the chill and assume you're ambitious at their expense. New friends may not get a second chance. Soften one thing. Ask a new person about something with no status attached, where they grew up or what they cook, and listen to the whole answer.

sun.upright:
Aquarius is the sign opposite Leo, and the Sun is in detriment there. It works against the grain in your sign, and the effort shows. That's worth knowing when this card lands on an Aquarius Sun, because it's a Sun card, all about a self built on what it holds, and your Sun is built differently. You'd sooner belong to an idea, a group, a cause, than to a pile of things. So a card about keeping what's yours can feel faintly embarrassing.

Saturn is the thread between you. It rules Capricorn and it's also the traditional ruler of Aquarius, so the card's sign and yours share a landlord, even as neighbours with little else in common. Air and earth don't agree about much, one deals in ideas and the other wants proof. In practice your grip is on independence. You hold on to not needing anyone, to your own way of doing things, to principles you've stopped testing. It feels like integrity, and sometimes it is. Sometimes it's a way of hoarding yourself, keeping a partner or a team from having any real claim on you.

At work it's the brilliant colleague who won't share the method. In love it's keeping your own flat, your own money, your own plans, long after the relationship would like some of them joined. With friends it's being loyal to the group while giving very little of yourself to any one person in it. Take one principle you hold rigidly and test it against the last year. Keep it if it's still true.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with the Four reversed may be giving itself away to causes. The volunteering, the group, the friend's project, all taking the hours and money you'd set aside for your own life. The Sun in detriment finds it hard to put its own interests first. The other version is a hard, detached independence, refusing any help, any sharing, any compromise, and calling it freedom. Either way you end up feeling slightly apart, which you'll say you like.

Friends and causes show the first. Partners feel the second. Look honestly at where your time and money went last month, and whose life they were spent on. Then put one evening, or one amount, back into something that's only for you.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon feels safe with a bit of distance. Space to think, friends who don't crowd you, a life where nobody tells you how to feel. This card on your tides is about holding close, and the Sun, in detriment in Aquarius, doesn't sit easily here. Its warmth has to work against the grain of your Moon. So what you're likely to feel is a guarded, slightly cold version of your usual detachment.

Capricorn and Aquarius are next-door signs that don't have much in common, yet they share Saturn as ruler, which is why the reserve feels so familiar and so hard to shift. Air and earth pull against each other. You know exactly what you think about your feelings and very little about the feelings themselves. You'll explain calmly why something doesn't bother you. It might, a lot. The card's grip is on your emotional independence, and the fear under it is of needing someone and being let down.

With a partner it's pulling back just when things are going well. With friends it's being the one everyone confides in and confiding in nobody. With sleep it's the mind that won't switch off, running through a problem as if it belonged to someone else. When a friend next asks how you are, give them one sentence that starts with 'I feel'.
moon.reversed:
Reversed on an Aquarius Moon, the Four can freeze feeling solid. The Sun's in detriment in your Moon sign, and when this card turns over its warmth goes missing altogether. You go logical, efficient and distant, keeping everyone at the same polite length, and you'd honestly struggle to say what you're feeling if asked. Or, less often, there's a rush of neediness you're embarrassed by, clinging to a friend or partner and then withdrawing hard.

Friends might notice you've gone quiet in the group chat. A partner might feel they're living with a flatmate. Pick someone you trust and tell them, in plain words, that you've been keeping your distance. You don't have to explain why.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising tends to come across as friendly but a little removed, interested in everyone and hard to get close to. Draw this card for your mask and the removed part does most of the work. People meet someone cool, clever and self-contained, with opinions they'll share and a private life they won't. The Sun is in detriment in your rising sign, so the card's planet doesn't bring much warmth to the door.

There's a bit of chart logic behind that. With Aquarius rising, Leo sits on your seventh house, where partners and close allies live, and the Sun rules Leo. So the card's planet struggles at your front door and is completely at home in the people who come towards you. You may find yourself drawn to warm, expressive types, and holding them at a distance while you decide whether to trust them. Saturn rules both Capricorn and Aquarius in the old system, and it gives you the same reserve the card has. To you it just feels like being careful with your time.

In a job interview it reads as independent and a little unusual, which some panels love. In a new friendship it's the person who's great company at the pub and impossible to pin down for a weekend. In dating it's warm people finding you intriguing and hard work. Accept the next invitation that involves some commitment, a whole day or a trip, and let someone see you with your guard down for a few hours.
rising.reversed:
An Aquarius Ascendant with the card reversed can come across as aloof to the point of rudeness. You're polite, you're interested in the idea being discussed, and you give the person nothing, and they go home feeling dismissed. The Sun's in detriment on your Ascendant, and upside down this card can make it seem there's no warmth at the door at all. Or you swing the other way, laying out your principles and theories in a first meeting until people feel lectured.

At work it's the new colleague who finds you impossible to read. At a party it's the conversation that turned into a debate. Ask the next stranger something personal, where they're from or what they love doing, and follow it with a second question.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns give. Time, money, sympathy, a spare bed, the last of the biscuits, sometimes more of yourself than you really had. This card on your light is about holding on to what's yours, and for a Pisces Sun that's a skill worth borrowing. Capricorn is sextile Pisces, a friendly angle that still has to be used, and water and earth give each other shape. So the card doesn't fight you. It offers you a container.

The Sun comes into Pisces as Jupiter's guest, or Neptune's if you use the modern ruler, and both of those widen things, blur things, give things away. That's where the tension is. Holding on can feel selfish to you, even unkind. Someone asks and you say yes before you've checked your own diary or your own balance. What the card wants is enough kept back that you can go on giving without running dry, and a lot of Pisces Suns only learn that after they've run dry once or twice.

With money it's the loan to a friend you'll never see again, and the savings that would stop you needing one yourself. At work it's the extra shift, the favour, the unpaid help, and a creative project of your own that never gets the hours. Pisces' own card is The Moon, all tides and half-light, and this one asks for something you can see and count. Set up one account, or one hour a week, that belongs to you and doesn't get given away.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun with this card upside down can leak. Money goes out in small sympathetic amounts, a donation, a round, a friend's rent just this once, until you're the one who's short. The Sun, under Jupiter or Neptune here, loses its edges. Or, less often, a Pisces Sun gets frightened and clutches, hoarding in secret, hiding purchases, leaving the post unopened. Either version is about boundaries that have gone soft.

The unopened post is a good place to start. Open it, all of it, with a cup of tea and someone kind sitting nearby. Then decide one thing you'll stop paying for, whether it's a subscription or somebody else's habit.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks everything up. Other people's moods, the news, a sad song in a café. Feeling safe means having somewhere to retreat to and enough quiet to let it all drain out again. The Four turning up in your tides is about holding firm, and here it's showing you trying to build some walls, which for a Pisces Moon is new and a bit uncomfortable.

Capricorn sextiles Pisces, and the two elements are on good terms, each giving the other shape, so there's help in this. The card offers you edges, and a Pisces Moon without edges tends to wake up exhausted from other people's problems. Keeping something back can feel like shutting a door on someone who needs you, and you'll hear yourself apologising for it. The Sun visits your Moon sign as Jupiter's guest, generous and expansive, so the pull to give is strong. Holding a little back, a night, an hour, a bit of money, is how the card suggests you look after yourself.

In your sleep it can show as dreams heavy with other people's troubles. With a friend who leans on you it's the phone you've started letting ring out, and the guilt that follows. Money-wise, it might be the first time you've kept a proper buffer. Keep one evening a week that nobody else gets, and tell people it's taken.
moon.reversed:
The Four reversed on a Pisces Moon is either no walls at all or walls in the wrong place. You're taking on everyone's feelings, lending money you need, staying up for someone else's crisis. The Sun, Jupiter's guest in your sign, is generous to a fault, and when the card turns over the generosity has nothing to stop it. Or you've gone the other way and shut everything out in secret, curtains drawn, phone off, the comfort things done alone.

Your body will tell you which. Heavy tiredness is the first, a strange flatness the second. With a partner it might look like drifting into their moods until you can't find yours. Tell one person which it is. Ask them to check on you in a week, and let them.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising usually comes across as soft, open and easy to talk to, the stranger people tell their life story to on a train. With this card drawn for your mask there's a firmer edge to that. People still find you kind, but they notice you're keeping something back, and it makes you seem steadier, better defended. Capricorn is sextile Pisces and earth and water suit each other, so it fits you better than you'd think.

The Sun visits your sign as a guest of Jupiter, or Neptune in modern terms, which keeps some warmth in the reserve. You're not saying yes to everything in the first five minutes, for once. That might be because you've been burned. With Pisces rising, Virgo is on your seventh house, and Virgo is trine Capricorn. So the people you're dealing with may be practical, careful, a bit exacting, and you're meeting them on their terms, which is new for you and quite good for you.

At work this is a real help, because it stops you being handed everybody's problems on day one. With a new friend it means they meet someone with limits, which is healthier for you both. With a pushy salesperson it might be the first time you've walked out without buying anything. Keep one thing about yourself private at the next introduction, and notice that people like you just as much.
rising.reversed:
When Pisces rising draws this card reversed, the edges tend to blur. You give too much away too soon, your number, your time, your sympathy, and a stranger is leaning on you by the end of the evening. Jupiter's generosity runs straight through your front door with the card upside down. Or you go the opposite way and seem vague and closed, hard to reach, as if you're somewhere else entirely.

At work it's being volunteered for everything because you look like you won't mind. In dating it's attaching quickly to someone who hasn't earned it. Before the next first meeting, decide on one thing you won't offer, a favour or a phone number, and hold to it for the evening.

1.upright:
Body, bearing, the way you walk into a room and the way you start anything, that's first house territory. With the Four of Pentacles here the whole stance goes defensive. You're holding yourself in, shoulders up, arms close, and people read that before you've said a word. It's an angular house, a corner of the chart, so whatever's here tends to be visible and to get things done.

The Sun is exalted in Aries, and Aries is this house's natural sign, so the card's planet is welcome here and does well. That gives you presence. The square from Capricorn to Aries adds friction, though, because the first house wants to begin and this card wants to hold. You might feel ready to start something and unwilling to risk anything to do it, wanting every piece in place before you put yourself forward. It can feel very sensible and slightly stuck, both at once.

Your body is the most literal place this shows, tension carried in the jaw and the hands, sometimes a stiffness you notice getting out of bed. In a new job or a new project it's a cautious start, well prepared and quite guarded. With your image it may be spending carefully on clothes or a haircut that make you look like someone to take seriously. Loosen your posture on purpose once a day, drop the shoulders, unclench the hands, and see whether your thinking follows.
1.reversed:
In the first house, the reversed Four tends to show in how you carry yourself. Either you've locked up, so guarded in your manner that people find you hard to approach, or you've let your own upkeep go, the sleep, the meals, the basic looking after yourself, because you've been spending yourself on everything else. Aries sits naturally on this house and squares the card's sign, so the tension goes straight into the body.

A new start may stall because you won't put resources behind it. Your health habits may slide. A friend might say you seem tense, or that you've looked tired for a while. Choose one physical thing that's yours, a walk, a proper breakfast, a haircut, and give it to yourself regularly without negotiating.

2.upright:
The second house is money in the plain sense, what's in your account and what you earn, and it's also your sense of what you're worth. The Four of Pentacles is about as at home here as a card can be. Taurus is the natural sign, Capricorn is trine to it, and all of it is earth, so the card speaks the house's own language and turns it up, the good and the excessive both. It's a succedent house too, the kind that consolidates and holds.

So it's a strong stretch for saving, paying down, building a buffer. You'll feel the pull to protect what you've got, and it's mostly wise. The thing to watch is how closely your self-worth is tied to the number. When the balance goes up you feel steadier as a person. When it drops, even for a good reason, you feel smaller. That's the grip the card pictures, and it doesn't feel like greed at all. It feels like finally being safe.

In your finances it's a good time to set up the automatic transfer, check your super or pension, and clear the small debts. With your earnings it's asking for a raise on the strength of what you've already delivered, and holding your number. With spending, notice where caution has turned into never buying yourself anything good. When did you last buy yourself something well made that wasn't on sale?
2.reversed:
In the second house the reversed Four tends to swing between clutching and leaking. You're either checking your balance constantly and refusing any spending at all, or money's slipping away in small amounts you don't track, comfort purchases, forgotten subscriptions, lending you don't mention. Venus runs Taurus, the sign that belongs to this house, so comfort and pleasure get tangled up in it. Underneath both is how safe you feel about your own worth.

The bank statement is the honest record. Sit down with three months of it and a highlighter, and if you share money with a partner, do it together. Mark what you'd happily spend again and what you wouldn't. Change one thing, and leave the rest alone for a while.

3.upright:
Everyday talk lives in the third house. Messages, siblings, neighbours, the short trips you make on repeat, and whatever you're learning. The Four of Pentacles here is careful with its words and keeps things to itself.
